content_text: [1/2 @gregoryblotnick] re: DM on stock pitch competitions "where should I start" -- best 80/20 type answer I've got: model to consensus, determine which 1-3 KPI's you may have a variant view...and then primary research drives the bus from there. "What work have you done to support your opinion?" that's the operative question to keep asking yourself re: any variance from consensus that's why this is 80/20. any pitch that takes a variant view, and has a mountain of primary research supporting KPI's vs consensus...like, there's no universe in which that pitch won't be viewed favorably. --- [2/2 @gregoryblotnick] I say 80/20 because otherwise, a question like "how should I do a stock pitch," you get 50,000 people weighing in and each gives a 20 page answer, and the person ends up more confused than when they started LLM's are helpful but you always have that nagging feeling of "is this how professionals do it" (which was literally how he asked it), because LLMs sometimes are off base on tone or verbiage Far better to say "if you nail these 3 things, it's almost impossible to fuck the rest up." Like, the pitch should write itself after model/KPI/variance to consensus is done...
